clue.text: England's captain, once one of several scorers

definitions.meaning: Andrew ... captained the England cricket team from 2009 to 2012
the ... family of Vienna (Johann father and son, Josef, Eduard) all wrote musical scores

explanation.surface: A former England cricket captain was one of several batsmen who scored runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorers' suggests cricket after 'captain', but here it means people who write musical scores, composers.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to a former cricket captain and to a family of Viennese composers.

clue.text: Visit Bill Oddie's top bird

parts.note: to tour a place is to visit it
AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bill Oddie, the British TV birdwatcher, is invited to come and see a prize bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Oddie is a well-known British birdwatcher and TV presenter, so 'Bill' looks like part of his name; it is AC, for account.
explanation.definitionFit: The touraco is a colourful African bird, a species of turaco.

clue.text: Needed top card holding hearts and diamonds

indicators.note: holding means the top card wraps around the hearts letter

parts.note: the ace is the highest card in many games
H is the bridge abbreviation for hearts
D is the bridge abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player needed an ace to go with a hand full of red suits.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ached for something is to have yearned for or needed it.

clue.text: Turning over while American's boxing — wrestling ring punch

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the earlier pieces surround the next
turning over means the word for while is read backwards

parts.note: as can mean while (as I was leaving)
A is a standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: wrestling suggests struggling and twisting, so the letters of ring are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American boxer turns over while a wrestler throws a punch in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a boxing blow, matching the ring and wrestling, but it is the Spanish drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish wine punch with fruit, a mixed drink served from a bowl.

clue.text: Leave his prey to perish in 25

indicators.note: something left to perish breaks down, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A predator lets its victim die, here in a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25 refers to 25-down, the theme word for these reptiles; 'in' just links the anagram to it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small venomous pit reptile of Central America, named for scales above its eyes.

clue.text: "Yes, '70s prog rock band Queen", one cries

parts.note: ELP is Emerson, Lake and Palmer, a 1970s progressive rock band
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out the names of rock bands Yes and Queen from the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes and Queen were both real 1970s rock bands, so the solver reads all three as band names; only the middle one is.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a sharp cry, so someone who gives one is a crier.

clue.text: Record dovetailing IBM company with British type of computer virus

parts.note: a log is a record

indicators.note: dovetailing means interlocking, so the letters are fitted together in a new order

explanation.surface: A record of IBM merging with a British firm describes a computer virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dovetailing' scrambles the company letters to give ICBOMB, so the IBM in the surface is fodder rather than the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Malicious code set to trigger damage when certain conditions are met is known by this two-word name.

clue.text: What I try to do should be OK?

definitions.meaning: the setter, speaking as I, aims to compose clues that play fair with the solver
a barometer reading or forecast of settled fine weather means things should be fine

explanation.surface: The setter hopes their efforts turn out acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as the setter talking about setting fair clues; the second is the weather term for settled conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a weather forecast term for settled conditions and also describes setting clues fairly.

clue.text: 25 dished out more cold bacon

indicators.note: food dished out is served up and spread around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone serves extra chilled bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25 refers to 25-down, the theme reptile; the answer is an Asian species with a ring marking on its hood.
explanation.definitionFit: This Asian venomous reptile is named for the single ring marking on its hood, like an eyeglass.

clue.text: Former president getting head from Monica — a second short spell in White House 25

parts.note: George Bush, either father or son, was a US president

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a president serves a term, a spell of office, in the White House

explanation.surface: A former US president has another brief term, with a nod to Monica Lewinsky.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Clinton scandal; the 25 refers to 25-down, the theme reptile, a large pit viper of the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large venomous pit viper of Central and South America.

clue.text: Sign forms — how final couple to hotel are written down in evenings?

indicators.note: in means the second piece is placed inside the word for evenings

parts.note: nights are evenings

parts.words: how final couple to hotel are written down
parts.note: the last two letters of hotel are E and L; written in a down entry, E sits on L, giving E ON L

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a hotel sign looks at night.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry one letter sits on top of the next, so E written above L is 'E on L'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing gas-tube signs are a common form of illuminated advertising sign.

clue.text: Run large 25

parts.note: 25 refers to 25-down; an adder is one such reptile

explanation.surface: Looks like an instruction to run a large reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: A run in a stocking or tights is called a ladder in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a run in tights is a ladder.

clue.text: Patent protecting firm — origin of Apple Mac?

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the patent word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: patent means obvious, overt
CO, for company, is a firm

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A patent protects a firm, and the question is whether it covers Apple's Mac computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Patent and Apple Mac point to technology, but Mac is short for mackintosh, a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh, or mac, is a waterproof coat worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Tricks 16 artist

parts.note: cons are tricks or swindles
16 refers to 16-across, whose word also means a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: An artist plays tricks with a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was an English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English Romantic landscape painter, famous for The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Sugar's replacement upset on news, outside, hot from The Apprentice's final

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means the whole assembly is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: outside means news goes around the next pieces
from means the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: final means the last letter

explanation.surface: Alan Sugar, host of The Apprentice, is upset to be replaced as the news breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Sugar hosts the UK version of The Apprentice, but here sugar is the food. The assembled letters RENETEEWS are turned upside down by 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial products used in place of sugar in drinks and food go by this name.

clue.text: 25 to drive over playing surface featuring 25s and 12s?

parts.note: 25 refers to 25-down; a boa is one such reptile

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for drive, as in street names

explanation.surface: A reptile drives across a game board covered with reptiles and ladders.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the board for the children's game snakes and ladders.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's game of reptiles and climbing rungs is played on a squared board.

clue.text: See 5
Independent supplement dropping extreme characters for picture

indicators.note: the extreme characters of the alphabet are A and Z, which are dropped

parts.note: a newspaper supplement is a magazine

explanation.surface: A newspaper supplement drops its outer letters to make room for a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extreme characters' suggests the ends of the word, but here it means the ends of the alphabet, A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form it in the mind, to envisage it.

clue.text: One doing routine work round large-sized breasts — plastic surgery piece

parts.note: O is round in shape
DD is a large bra cup size
a job is slang for cosmetic surgery, as in a nose job
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A surgeon doing breast enlargements as routine work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like cosmetic surgery; 'piece' is a draughts or chess man.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman doing small routine tasks around the house goes by this hyphenated name.

clue.text: Bad singer

parts.note: Bad is a 1987 album and single by Michael ..., so its singer is ...

explanation.walkthrough: It seems to mean an untalented singer, but Bad is a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Jackson recorded the hit album and song titled Bad.

clue.text: Ring-shaped forms unreasonable — not unusually obese

indicators.note: forms means the letters of unreasonable are reshaped
not means the letters of obese, rearranged, are taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: A ring-shaped figure seems unreasonable, as does being unusually obese.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of OBESE from UNREASONABLE and rearrange the remaining seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular is the formal adjective for things shaped like a ring.

clue.text: See 10
Co-star at bad singer

indicators.note: bad means the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor complains about a poor singer playing opposite them.
explanation.walkthrough: A castrato is a male singer castrated before puberty to keep a high voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrato is a male soprano or alto singer of the baroque era.

clue.text: Function pictures, having airbrushed mother, capturing Oscars

indicators.note: capturing means the shortened pictures word encloses the next piece
having airbrushed means having removed the mother

parts.note: the pictures is the cinema
MA is mother
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet, so Oscars are OS

explanation.surface: Film pictures win Oscars after a mother is airbrushed out of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having airbrushed' gives CINE; Oscars, a plural, is the NATO letter O plus the plural S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosine is a trigonometric function of an angle.

clue.text: Racer, perhaps, briefly exposed following its profile?

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the profile letter

parts.note: the side view of a coiled reptile looks like the letter S

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: naked means exposed

explanation.surface: A racer is caught exposed, briefly, with only its profile showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racer' suggests a driver, but racers are a family of fast North American reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Racers are fast slender non-venomous reptiles of North America, an example of the type.

clue.text: Bad US singer at musical introductions

indicators.note: bad means the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor American singer performs at a show's opening numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Key and time signatures are printed at the start of a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Key and time signatures are written at the very start of a musical stave.

clue.text: Friend is friendly — not initially

indicators.note: not initially means without its first letter

parts.note: pally means friendly

explanation.surface: A friend is someone friendly, though not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend or supporter on your side is one of your allies.

clue.text: Fears tense mistakes

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
errors are mistakes

explanation.surface: A nervous writer fears making errors of tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrors are great fears, the plural noun matching the plural fears.

clue.text: Makes beloved Kennedy et al rise regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: The Kennedys and their circle rise steadily in public affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them loved or liked.
